text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Dedicated pool dp-eu-3 (eu-west-1) queue depth spiked. 20x baseline RPS for last 6m, per-token tail latency >3s, queued requests ~1.2k. Autoscaler not scaling. Paging oncall.

maria: Oncall (maria) here — looking. Any indication of failed scale actions in autoscaler logs?

jun: I'm seeing repeated 429s from cluster controller when trying to create nodes, error: `quota_exceeded: insufficient-gpu-alloc` in the control plane logs. Pulling autoscaler logs now.

phil: If quota_exceeded is real, plan B is to enable burst capacity and shift lower-priority tenants off dp-eu-3. We should also apply soft RPS caps for heavy customers to protect system.

anya: Agree. I'll prep a quick traffic shaping patch for the API gateway to impose per-customer soft limits. Which customers look like the largest contributors?

jun: Top callers right now: cust-711 (40% of surge), cust-999 (18%), anonymous-batch (15%). cust-711 looks like a new integration loop.

phil: Recommend immediate mitigations:
1) Enable burst capacity for dp-eu-3 for 30m
2) Add soft rate-limit for cust-711 to 25 RPS
3) Evict non-critical background jobs on that pool

Here's the internal command for burst toggle (use with ops escalation):
```bash
# enable burst for 30 minutes
redwoodctl pools toggle-burst --pool dp-eu-3 --enable --duration 30m --reason "live surge: autoscale quota_exceeded"
```

And API gateway patch (one-liner):
```bash
apictl rate-limit apply --scope customer --id cust-711 --limit 25 --burst 50 --duration 30m --reason "protect cluster during surge"
```

maria: I'm going to enable burst now (will run with oncall privilege). Will also mark impacted nodes as "no-new-sessions" while we rebalance.

ops-bot: ACTION_START: redwoodctl pools toggle-burst --pool dp-eu-3 --enable --duration 30m --user maria

ops-bot: ACTION_RESULT: success — burst capacity added +6 GPUs to dp-eu-3. Pool qlen reduced to ~320 in 90s.

jun: Nice, queue dropped to ~300, tail p99 latency down to 1.1s. Still seeing high allocation failures for a couple customers but much improved overall.

anya: Applying soft rate-limit to cust-711 now.

ops-bot: ACTION_START: apictl rate-limit apply --scope customer --id cust-711 --limit 25 --duration 30m --user anya
ops-bot: ACTION_RESULT: success — cust-711 limited to 25 RPS (soft). 429 rate from cust-711 decreased by 88%.

lydia-cs: CS update: pinged primary contact at cust-711, they acknowledged a broken retry loop in their integration and will throttle on their side. They requested an ETA — told them we applied protective limits and will follow up after stabilization.

maria: Good. I'm going to hand off monitoring & next 15m mitigation to Jun while I take the next on-call rotation break. Jun, please escalate to infra-sre if quota_exceeded persists after burst expires.

jun: Got it. I'll keep dashboards and runbook open. If autoscaler still errors when burst ends, plan is to request emergency quota bump with infra and extend burst or migrate customers.

phil: Capture these items for post-incident:
- root cause investigation: why autoscaler hit quota_exceeded
- why background eviction didn't free enough capacity earlier
- improve runbook commands for one-click customer-rate-limits

maria: Agreed. I'll open the incident in the tracker (INC-2026-142) and tag infra, autoscaler, and cs for follow-up. For now marking incident as mitigated — surge handled with burst+rate-limits. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — Mitigated. Monitor for recurrences for next 2 hours. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-pool-surge

jun: I'll continue watch for 2h and close handoff note in the incident ticket. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
